claims.answer: Air is reachable through the Air app on macOS, Linux and Windows, Air Teams in the browser, and Air in JetBrains IDEs through an EAP plugin. The Air in IDEs page now says Air Teams on mobile is coming November 15; native-app versus mobile-browser delivery remains unestablished. A separate CLI surface is not established by the Air help.

desktop_os.answer: macOS (download or Toolbox), Linux (install script or Toolbox) and Windows (Toolbox) per the install page (2026-09-30). The July 2026 post (date from URL path) links Windows x64 and ARM64 downloads whose URLs carry type=preview.

mobile_apps.answer: The product page says Air Teams on mobile is coming November 15. It does not establish a shipped native app, minimum OS or store route as of November 7.

browser.answer: Air Teams runs in the browser at air.jetbrains.cloud and is the only surface with all features; the product page still invites early-access sign-up and rollout is gradual.

mobile_browser.answer: The mobile announcement does not distinguish phone-browser delivery from a native app; shipped mobile-browser support remains unknown.

cli.answer: The product page names Air Gateway as a CLI surface and the Console names the Central CLI. The checked Air help does not establish Air Gateway setup or commands.

editor_extensions.answer: Air in JetBrains IDEs is the Air plugin: installed from JetBrains Marketplace on 2026.2 IDE versions (slug air-alpha) and bundled in 2026.3 EAP builds; it works in all JetBrains IDEs except Android Studio. The EAP post calls it an EAP release.

task_actions.answer: Cloud tasks can be started from the browser, the Air app and IntelliJ-based IDEs; the browser can comment on diffs and stop the agent. The browser is the only surface with everything: automations are managed in the browser (automations, 2026-09-30), and the Air app help says projects, automations, environment configurations, connectors and repository access stay in the browser. No per-client action matrix is published.

notifications.answer: The Air app notifies when a task needs input (Open Task); Air in IDEs shows header counters for sessions waiting for input, processing or recently completed, with an optional Caps Lock LED signal on compatible macOS keyboards; automations can send notifications including outgoing webhooks. Browser or mobile push notifications are not documented.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Tasks started in the IDE can be followed in the browser or Air app, and the IDE session tree lists cloud runs from the web or another machine. The Air in IDEs product page separately announces Air Teams mobile for November 15; current mobile availability and delivery type are not established.

limitations: Air in IDEs is EAP (Marketplace plugin air-alpha for 2026.2 IDEs, bundled in 2026.3 EAP builds, not Android Studio); Air Teams is offered to JetBrains business customers and cloud runs are rolling out gradually; some features need a JetBrains AI subscription or AI seats.
Windows: the install page documents Toolbox install; the July 2026 post links Windows x64 and ARM64 downloads with type=preview in the URL. No hands-on run.
The product page names Air Gateway as a CLI surface; its setup and command contract were not established in the Air help pass.

Agent lineup statements differ by surface: the October 2026 Air in IDEs EAP post says "Air supports Codex, Gemini, GitHub Copilot, Claude Agent, and Junie out of the box", while supported-agents (2026-10-01), which covers Air Teams and the Air app, lists Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie, and Copilot is added in the Air app as an ACP agent. claims.answer: The Air help lists a four-agent lineup for Air Teams and the Air app: Claude Agent, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie; Gemini CLI is temporarily unavailable for cloud tasks. The Air app also runs ACP agents added through acp.json, such as GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi and Cline; acp.json agents are not available in Air Teams cloud. A JetBrains announcement dated 2026-11-03 adds GitHub Copilot (the Copilot CLI over ACP) as a selectable agent in Air in IDEs and in Air Teams cloud tasks and automations, running on the user's Copilot plan; the help pages do not yet document this. Air in IDEs connects agents through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

harnesses.answer: Air includes Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie with surface restrictions, plus local ACP agents including OpenCode and Pi. model_providers.answer: Providers are Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and the JetBrains AI provider; model and effort are chosen per task and local models are reachable through an agent that supports them (Ollama or LM Studio via ACP). No provider list beyond the agent vendors is published in the help.

custom_adapters.answer: Any installed ACP-compatible agent can be added through acp.json in the Air app; acp.json agents are explicitly not available in Air Teams cloud tasks or the browser. GitHub Copilot reaches the cloud as a JetBrains-integrated agent, not through acp.json.

session_integration.answer: The Air in IDEs help says agents communicate with the plugin through ACP, the Air app runs any installed ACP agent like the built-in ones, and the IDE session tree also lists sessions started in external tools such as the Codex app. Whether the built-in agents are embedded harnesses or ACP adapters is not stated.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Different tasks can use different agents and a review pass can use a different agent than the author, but the agent and provider cannot change once a task has started.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Air app local tasks: a ChatGPT Plus, Pro or Team account for Codex and a Google Account (Personal or Workspace) for Gemini CLI (supported-agents 2026-10-01). Claude Pro, Max or Team for Claude Agent is unresolved: ai-credits (2026-09-30), quick-start and the own-account paragraph of supported-agents name it as an own subscription for local tasks, but the supported-agents Claude Agent row says "To use Claude Agent, connect your Anthropic Console account with API billing". Docker tasks cannot use a Claude subscription (ai-credits, run-environments). Air in IDEs: a Claude subscription cannot authorize Claude Agent in the chat surface; to use it, run Claude Code in the terminal surface. A GitHub Copilot subscription can run Copilot in Air in IDEs and in Air Teams cloud tasks (2026-11-03 announcement).

api_accounts.answer: Local Air app tasks can use the user's own API billing account (BYOK) for Anthropic, OpenAI or Google; Air in IDEs accepts Anthropic API-key authentication with API billing for Claude Agent.

vendor_credits.answer: Per the help, cloud tasks and automations spend JetBrains AI credits, and JetBrains AI can also serve local tasks. Exception per the 2026-11-03 announcement: GitHub Copilot cloud tasks and automation runs use the user's Copilot plan, which Air neither tracks nor limits.

local_models.answer: A local model runner such as Ollama or LM Studio connects through an ACP-compatible agent (July 2026 release post); the Air app respects the agent's model settings. Setup is not described as a built-in model picker.

account_switching.answer: Air in IDEs selects the authorization source per session and lets the user pick another source in the session; the product page says users can switch subscriptions mid-session. The Air app uses a connected own account before JetBrains AI credits.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: Local use needs a connected provider account or agent login and no JetBrains AI subscription; Air in IDEs needs no login until an agent is authorized and Junie Lite needs a JetBrains Account. Cloud runs need a JetBrains Account and a JetBrains AI subscription or AI seats.

provider_restrictions.answer: Docker tasks cannot use a Claude subscription because the subscription credentials stay on the machine; agents added through acp.json use their own subscriptions and a Claude Free, Pro or Max subscription does not work with them; own accounts do not apply to cloud tasks or automations; a Claude subscription cannot authorize Claude Agent in the Air in IDEs chat surface; JetBrains AI cannot be an authorization source in China (Air in IDEs).

limitations: Per the help, direct provider subscriptions and BYOK apply to local tasks only and cloud tasks and automations use JetBrains AI credits; the 2026-11-03 announcement makes GitHub Copilot the exception (Copilot plan in cloud), which the help pages do not yet document.

Unresolved for the Air app: whether Claude Agent accepts a Claude Pro, Max or Team subscription. The supported-agents Claude Agent row names only Console API billing and states no local or non-Docker exception; ai-credits, quick-start and the own-account paragraph of supported-agents name the subscription for local tasks, and ai-credits and run-environments exclude it in Docker. No hands-on sign-in was tested.
